definitions.explanation: A sensory perception that appears real but is created by the mind, occurring without any actual external stimulus. Can be visual, auditory, or involve other senses.

examples.japanese: {高熱|こうねつ}で{幻覚|げんかく}を{起|お}こした。
{睡眠|すいみん}{不足|ぶそく}が{続|つづ}くと、{幻覚|げんかく}{症状|しょうじょう}が{出|で}ることがある。
examples.english: Prolonged sleep deprivation can cause hallucination symptoms.

notes:
FORMS:
{幻|げん} (illusion, phantom) + {覚|かく} (sense, perception)

TYPES:
- {視覚|しかく}{幻覚|げんかく}: visual hallucination
- {聴覚|ちょうかく}{幻覚|げんかく}: auditory hallucination ({幻聴|げんちょう} is more common for this)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {幻聴|げんちょう}: auditory hallucination (hearing voices)
- {幻想|げんそう}: fantasy, illusion (not pathological)
- {錯覚|さっかく}: optical illusion, misperception

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幻覚|げんかく}が{見|み}える: to see hallucinations
- {幻覚|げんかく}を{起|お}こす: to experience hallucinations
- {幻覚|げんかく}{症状|しょうじょう}: hallucination symptoms
- {幻覚|げんかく}{作用|さよう}: hallucinogenic effect
